overview: This single-page file index concerns immigration regulation in Formosa (Taiwan). It lists correspondence from Hsinchu and Tokyo dated November 16 and 17, including Tokyo telegram no. 943, and points to information on Taiwan’s rules for the temporary admission and residence of foreign musicians, actors, artists, choristers, and other aliens; the referenced item reportedly enclosed a copy and translation of regulations received from the U.S. vice consul in Taihoku (modern Taipei).

subfiles.title: List of papers: Immigration—Formosa
subfiles.about: An index records two items concerning Taiwan immigration regulations and directs researchers to related decimal-file references.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists a November 16 item from Hsinchu associated with Ketchum and Tokyo telegram no. 943 of November 17 associated with Garrels. Its purport describes information on immigration laws and regulations governing the temporary admission and residence in Taiwan of instrumental musicians, other musicians, actors, artists, choristers, and other aliens. It notes that the referenced correspondence enclosed a copy and translation of regulations received from the vice consul in Taihoku and supplies related file references, including 80.504/36, 894a.111, and 894a.504.

interest: The sheet is useful as a documentary finding aid because it identifies correspondence that may no longer be present in this bundle and connects it to related decimal-file classifications. Its unusually specific reference to regulations for itinerant performers illuminates the bureaucratic treatment of mobile entertainers and other foreign visitors in colonial Taiwan. It also preserves a consular transmission chain linking Hsinchu, Taihoku, and the U.S. diplomatic establishment in Tokyo.
